source.title: RoboMemArena: A Comprehensive and Challenging Robotic Memory Benchmark
source.authors: Huashuo Lei; Wenxuan Song; Huarui Zhang; Jieyuan Pei; Jiayi Chen; Haodong Yan; Han Zhao; Pengxiang Ding; Zhipeng Zhang; Lida Huang; Donglin Wang; Yan Wang; Haoang Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some table content is flattened, but the overall averages used here are identifiable.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares task performance across differently sized language-model backbones, a different measure and setting from the original held-out-loss scaling laws. This bears on downstream performance scaling (V6), but it does not measure language-model cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports robotic task success for PrediMem with Qwen3 backbones of different sizes and states that scaling up consistently improves performance under matched pretraining data and architecture. These results bear on V6 only; the paper does not test the claimed language-model loss laws or fit predictive scaling curves.
record.test_reason: Section 5.4 and Table 2(d) give robot task success for the PrediMem planner built on 1.7B, 4B and 8B Qwen3 backbones. That is a new setting (a fine-tuned robot planner) with a result on whether downstream performance rises with model size. Only three sizes are tested, no curve is fitted, and the result is not tied to pretraining loss. It bears weakly on V6 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors state that scaling the S2 backbone under matched pretraining data and architecture consistently improves performance across all tasks. They attribute this to stronger reasoning and memory capabilities in larger models. They fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a robotic benchmark-performance comparison across backbone sizes, not a held-out language-model cross-entropy sweep or fit of power laws; it does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.

fits_no_version.finding: Average CSR rises with keyframe-bank capacity (best uncapped) and peaks at a 3–5 frame recent window (Fig. 5a,b). These are memory-capacity sweeps, not model or data scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Performance of memory-augmented robot policies depends on memory-buffer capacity, with diminishing or negative returns past a window size.

record.problems: The scaling comparison covers three backbone sizes and reports no uncertainty estimates. It evaluates robotic task success rather than language-model pretraining loss, and it does not fit a curve or demonstrate quantitative predictability.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss is measured.
All: no fits and no extrapolation.
All: no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law form is fitted for this fine-tuning or robotics regime.
Quantitative predictability (fitted curve or extrapolation), any link to pretraining loss, and more than three sizes.

missing.what: Per-category TSR/CSR across backbone sizes; all are monotone in size (e.g. Occlusion TSR 7.3, 18.2, 27.3; Sequence TSR 50.0, 65.0, 72.5).

record.verdict_notes: The paper calls Section 5.4 'scaling laws', but it only shows a monotone three-point trend for a fine-tuned robot planner. Gains shrink at the top: +12.0 then +6.6 TSR points. No uncertainty is reported. Treat it as weak, setting-specific evidence for V6.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs' loss from fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds for other modalities or training regimes.

The study reports downstream robotic task performance across backbone sizes, but does not test whether it is quantitatively predictable from pretraining loss or a fitted scaling curve, or whether the relationship generalizes beyond this task and setup.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

relationships.condition: PrediMem S2 planner fine-tuned on RoboMemArena, backbones 1.7B to 4B to 8B, simulation averages
relationships.reason: Average TSR rises 19.9 to 31.9 to 38.5 and CSR rises 41.4 to 51.7 to 55.2; per-category values in Table 2(d) are also monotone (r1–r6). The support is weak: three points, no fit, and possible backbone confound.
relationships.display_finding: Average TSR increased from 19.9 to 31.9 to 38.5 and CSR from 41.4 to 51.7 to 55.2, with monotonic gains across categories despite possible backbone confounding.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PrediMem average task performance on RoboMemArena across the tested Qwen3 backbone sizes
reader_labels.reason: Both reported overall metrics increase from 1.7B to 4B to the 8B PrediMem model (TSR: 19.9%, 31.9%, 38.5%; CSR: 41.4%, 51.7%, 55.2%), supporting a scale-related downstream-performance trend in this setup (r1–r6).
